# Jafari-aligned crossed random-effects count models

**GENERATED by `scripts/report_jafari_crossed.py`. Never hand-edit -- re-run it.**

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-jafari-crossed-re-design.md`

Replicates the model class of Jafari et al. (*PLOS ONE* 2024,
doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0302960) under three PI directives of 2026-09-10:
random intercepts only; crossed random effects of **state** and **year**
(substituting time for Jafari's industry dimension, which this project has no
analogue for); and a best-fitting family chosen **independently per outcome**,
with no symmetry constraint. The zero-inflation component carries the same
predictors as the conditional component wherever that is estimable, and both
blocks are reported.

`glmmTMB` already estimated the two components in one joint likelihood, and
always did -- that part always matched Jafari. What differed was that the
previous ladder set `ziformula = ~1` where Jafari mirrors the full predictor
list, and that its reporter never printed a zero-inflation block. Both are
closed here; no new estimation machinery was required.

## What this arm is NOT comparable to

- **Not comparable to `docs/count_models_zinb.md`.** That arm mandates
  `(1 + time | state)`. These fixed effects are conditional on a different
  partition of the variance, so coefficients are not line-by-line comparable.
  Any comparison must name which arm it quotes.
- **Not comparable in magnitude to the published Tables 2/3.** Variance
  components here are on the **log link** scale; the published tables are on the
  `log(count + 1)` outcome scale. No percentage variance reduction is computed
  in this arm at all -- that needs a random-intercept-only refit series against
  a single Model-1 baseline, which this ladder does not produce. Deliberate gap.
- **The two windows are different measures, not a longer one.** WPS-view counts
  (2011-2021) run 2-3x establishments-view counts (2011-2019) and correlate
  ~0 from 2017 on.

## The binding constraint: zeros

A mirrored zero-inflation block at Model 3 carries up to 10 logistic
parameters. Only one cell has the zeros to identify them.


| Cell | N | Zeros | % | ZI tier reached by the selected family |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Inspections, 2011-2019 (establishments view) | 423 | 4 | 0.9% | full mirror (every conditional predictor) |
| Inspections, 2011-2021 (WPS view) | 506 | 7 | 1.4% | full mirror (every conditional predictor) |
| Violations, 2011-2019 (establishments view) | 378 | 7 | 1.9% | n/a (plain family) |
| Violations, 2011-2021 (WPS view) | 501 | 86 | 17.2% | full mirror (every conditional predictor) |


## Specification

```
conditional:  count ~ time + time2 + time3 [+ log_inspections]
                      + SPEND_APP_z + SPEND_WORK_z + lii_2017_z
                      + h2a_per_farmworker_z + dol_demand_met_pct_z + pct_flc_z
                      + (1 | state) + (1 | year)

zero-infl.:        ~ the richest estimable subset of the same predictors
```

`glmmTMB`, ML, `time = year - 2017`. **There is no random slope anywhere in
this arm and no random-effects fallback tier**: a family that fails at
`(1 | state) + (1 | year)` is reported as non-converged and excluded from
selection, never downgraded to a simpler structure.

The fixed cubic and `(1 | year)` deliberately coexist (PI direction). `time` is
an exact function of `year`, so the cubic is the smooth component and the year
random intercept the shrunk departure from it. Two consequences are reported
rather than hidden: the cubic can lose significance to the year effect, and
**sigma^2_year rests on 9 (2019) or 11 (2021) levels** -- at or below the
conventional minimum for a variance component. No claim here rests on
sigma^2_year alone.

**COVID is not fit as an indicator.** `(1 | year)` absorbs the pandemic shock
by construction, so a 2020-21 dummy would compete with the term that already
contains it. The 2020 and 2021 year BLUPs are reported instead. They are **not**
comparable to the other arms' COVID coefficients.

### Zero-inflation tier ladder

ZI predictors are always a **subset** of the conditional predictors. That keeps
one analytic sample per (cell, model), which is what makes AIC comparable
across tiers. Within a family the ladder takes the richest tier that converges
cleanly (a fidelity rule, not an AIC rule); across families AIC picks the
winner, with each competitor's tier shown.

## Strength of the zero-inflated specifications

Matched comparisons only: same cell, same model, same analytic sample, both converged, neither degenerate nor collapsed. A positive margin means the zero-inflated family wins.

| ZI family | vs. plain family | Record | AIC margin range |
|---|---|---|---|
| ZI-NB1 | NB1 | 6-0 | +0.45 to +11.12 |
| ZI-NB1 | NB2 | 2-4 | -193.18 to +17.82 |
| ZI-NB1 | Poisson | 6-0 | +939.94 to +5248.49 |
| ZI-NB1 + ZI-RE | NB1 | 2-2 | -7.35 to +9.09 |
| ZI-NB1 + ZI-RE | NB2 | 1-3 | -200.97 to +10.07 |
| ZI-NB1 + ZI-RE | Poisson | 4-0 | +946.05 to +5240.69 |
| ZI-NB2 | NB1 | 6-0 | +70.70 to +224.96 |
| ZI-NB2 | NB2 | 6-0 | +15.21 to +83.53 |
| ZI-NB2 | Poisson | 6-0 | +1018.02 to +5473.00 |
| ZI-NB2 + ZI-RE | NB1 | 5-0 | +72.15 to +183.81 |
| ZI-NB2 + ZI-RE | NB2 | 5-0 | +14.83 to +111.57 |
| ZI-NB2 + ZI-RE | Poisson | 5-0 | +1018.85 to +4990.33 |
| ZIP | NB1 | 0-6 | -4988.79 to -868.61 |
| ZIP | NB2 | 0-6 | -5182.41 to -931.98 |
| ZIP | Poisson | 6-0 | +70.14 to +668.11 |


Against its **own** negative-binomial counterpart (the comparison that isolates inflation while holding the parameterisation fixed), a zero-inflated family wins **25 of 27** matched comparisons. This arm fits ZI-NB1 rungs, which the previous ladder did not, so an NB1 win is now tested against its own zero-inflated counterpart rather than winning by default.


## Model 3, Jafari Table 5 format

Significance: `***` p<.001, `**` p<.01, `*` p<.05, `+` p<.10. This is the project convention and differs in rendering from Jafari's own legend; the two tables should not be read against each other on stars alone. An em dash in the zero-inflated block means the term was **absent from the ZI formula** at the tier reached, not estimated at zero.

| Inspections, 2011-2019 (establishments view) | ZI-NB2 | 0.4938 | 0.0000 | -- | 7.8589 | 4 | 5.35 |
| Inspections, 2011-2021 (WPS view) | ZI-NB2 | 0.9162 | 0.0000 | -- | 4.8069 | 7 | 7.18 |
| Violations, 2011-2019 (establishments view) | NB2 | 0.3908 | 0.0307 | -- | 4.3908 | 7 | 23.21 |
| Violations, 2011-2021 (WPS view) | ZI-NB2 + ZI-RE | 0.7507 | 0.0000 | 2.4272 | 2.7314 | 86 | 78.14 |


`Dispersion` is theta for NB2 and a multiplier for NB1 -- **not** a residual variance. `sigma2_e` is null for every count fit here, deliberately.


### Structural-zero probability

The **sample mean** is the reportable figure: the mean over the analytic sample of each state-year's own zero-inflation probability, conditional on the fitted random effects. It is comparable to the observed zero rate beside it, because structural zeros are a subset of all zeros.

The last two columns are `plogis(b0)` and the Gauss-Hermite marginal `E[plogis(b0 + u)]`, and they are **n/a wherever the ZI block carries covariates** -- which under a mirrored ZI formula is most cells. Both evaluate the ZI linear predictor at x = 0, and with `log_inspections` (sample mean ~3.5, never z-scored) in the ZI block, x = 0 describes no state in the data. Computing them anyway is how an earlier draft of this memo reported a 0.46 structural-zero probability for a cell whose own model simulates 78 zeros in 501 rows. They are reported only at the `intercept` tier, where b0 is the entire ZI linear predictor.

| Cell | ZI tier | Pr(structural 0), **sample mean** | Obs. zero rate | Pr at median state | Pr marginal over u |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Inspections, 2011-2019 (establishments view) | mirror | **0.0094** | 0.0095 | n/a | n/a |
| Inspections, 2011-2021 (WPS view) | mirror | **0.0116** | 0.0138 | n/a | n/a |
| Violations, 2011-2021 (WPS view) | mirror | **0.1193** | 0.1717 | n/a | n/a |
